newsitem.title: UK: Catholic church in England to help priests' lovers.
newsitem.headline: Catholic church in England to help priests' lovers.

text.p: The Roman Catholic church in England and Wales is investigating how it can provide finanical help to women who have had affairs with priests, a bishop said on Friday.
The Bishop of Plymouth, Christopher Budd, said the church was responding to approaches made by women's groups and was looking into the issue in an "open-minded" way.
It has set up a team, which includes bishops and lay church members, to meet some of the women and consider help, including financial aid, for the priests' lovers and any children.
"We'll certainly see what can be done with regard to funding," the bishop told BBC radio.

The move by the Catholic Bishops Conference, which formulates policy for the church in England and Wales, follows a scandal last year over a bishop who ran off with a mother of three. Another woman then said the bishop had fathered her son.
Despite that controversy and repeated complaints from women's groups about sexism, Budd denied the church -- which forbids sexual relations for its priests -- was falling into disrepute.
He said a large number of priests were "faithful to their celibacy and go about their priestly ministry with all the difficulties of that."
